rubrics.justification: The response is broadly consistent with the provided 0DD grade, noting poor expansion and absent/degenerate ICM and TE, but it overstates certainty from the image alone and adds features like marked darkness/granularity and non-viability that may not be fully verifiable visually.

It begins to note the contrast between favorable patient factors and poor embryo quality, but the visible response is truncated and does not meaningfully integrate most clinical variables or their interaction with prognosis.
The reasoning shown is internally consistent in linking 0DD morphology to poor prognosis, but it is incomplete and somewhat absolute in calling the embryo non-viable without fuller nuance.

Use of Gardner terminology and recognition that DD morphology predicts very poor potential are generally aligned with IVF practice, but declaring the embryo definitively non-viable is stronger than standard evidence-based phrasing.
No concrete transfer recommendations, probability range, or future cycle planning are present in the visible response, so it offers little practical guidance.
